description: Composite two-panel figure linking solution-treatment temperature to austenite stability in Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C low-density steels. (a) Six vertically offset XRD profiles: x-axis 2θ/° spanning ~35° to 100° (ticks 40, 60, 80, 100) and y-axis Intensity/cps from 0 to 12000 (ticks every 2000); curves are labelled, bottom to top, 700°C, 800°C, 900°C (before deformation) and 700°C-F, 800°C-F, 900°C-F (after deformation). Reflections are indexed for austenite as ( 111), ( 200), ( 220), ( 311) and for ferrite as (110), (200), (211), with M3C2 marked near 2θ ≈ 41-42°; the austenite lines are strongest for 900°C and visibly weaker in the corresponding "-F" patterns. (b) Dual-axis plot with hatched bars on the left axis "The fraction of austenite(%)" (0-45) and a square-marker line on the right axis "Martensite transformation ratio/%" (0.0-1.0); x-axis "Steel" = H70, H80, H90. Bars give before-deformation austenite of 12.2, 20.7 and 33.8% against after-deformation 4.5, 5.8 and 3.4%; the line gives 0.631, 0.719 and 0.899. Together the panels demonstrate that increasing solution temperature raises the retained austenite fraction, which transforms more completely during tension.

subfigures.description: Stacked, intensity-offset XRD patterns (Intensity/cps vs 2θ/°) for the six conditions 700°C, 800°C, 900°C, 700°C-F, 800°C-F, 900°C-F. Peaks are indexed: austenite ( 111) ~43°, ( 200) ~50°, ( 220) ~74°, ( 311) ~89°; ferrite (110) ~44.6°, (200) ~65°, (211) ~82°; M3C2 carbide marked near 41-42°.

Dual-axis bar/line chart for steels H70, H80 and H90: hatched bars (legend: Before deformation, After deformation) read on the left axis 0-45% austenite fraction, printed 12.2/4.5, 20.7/5.8 and 33.8/3.4; a square-marker line reads on the right axis 0.0-1.0 martensite transformation ratio with printed values 0.631, 0.719 and 0.899.

observations.observation: Panel (a) stacks six XRD patterns labelled from bottom to top 700°C, 800°C, 900°C, 700°C-F, 800°C-F and 900°C-F, with the patterns vertically offset along an Intensity/cps axis reaching 12000.
Panel (a) x-axis is 2θ/° with tick labels 40, 60, 80 and 100, and the full displayed range runs from about 35° to 100°.
Reflections in panel (a) are indexed for austenite as ( 111), ( 200), ( 220), ( 311) and ( 222), and for ferrite as (110), (200), (211) and (220).
An M3C2 carbide reflection is labelled in panel (a) at about 2θ = 41-42°, adjacent to the ferrite (110) line.

Panel (b) has a left axis labelled 'The fraction of austenite(%)' from 0 to 45 (ticks every 5) and a right axis labelled 'Martensite transformation ratio/%' from 0.0 to 1.0 (ticks every 0.2), with x-axis categories H70, H80 and H90.
Before-deformation austenite fractions printed in panel (b) are 12.2% for H70, 20.7% for H80 and 33.8% for H90.
After-deformation austenite fractions printed in panel (b) are 4.5% for H70, 5.8% for H80 and 3.4% for H90.
The square-marker line in panel (b), read on the right axis, gives martensite transformation ratios of 0.631 (H70), 0.719 (H80) and 0.899 (H90).
The legend in panel (b) distinguishes the two bar hatching patterns as 'Before deformation' and 'After deformation'.
The caption states that the suffix '-F' denotes the state after fraction (i.e. after tensile deformation): 'F - after fraction'.

The caption states that panel (a) gives the XRD profiles and panel (b) the corresponding austenite fractions before and after tensile deformation, with the martensitic transformation ratios for the three steels also plotted in b.
The citing text asserts that in all steels the austenite volume fraction decreased after tensile tests, consistent with the lower 'After deformation' bars for H70, H80 and H90.

The citing text asserts that the martensite transformation ratio increased gradually as the solution temperature rose over 700-900 °C, with a peak value of 89.9% in H90, matching the printed right-axis value 0.899.
The citing text interprets the increasing transformation ratio as an enhanced TRIP effect associated with metastable austenite.
